name: 72-hour kit (Ready.gov basic)
source: Ready.gov, Build a Kit (public domain): https://www.ready.gov/kit
items: Water: 1 gallon (about 4 L) per person per day, for several days, for drinking and sanitation
Food: at least a several-day supply of non-perishable food
Battery-powered or hand-crank radio, and a NOAA Weather Radio with tone alert
Dust masks to help filter contaminated air
Plastic sheeting, scissors and duct tape to shelter in place
Moist towelettes, garbage bags and plastic ties for personal sanitation
Wrench or pliers to turn off utilities
Phone with chargers and a backup battery

name: Additional household items (Ready.gov)
source: Ready.gov, Build a Kit (public domain): https://www.ready.gov/kit
items: Soap, hand sanitizer and disinfecting wipes
Non-prescription medications: pain relievers, anti-diarrhea medication, antacids or laxatives
Prescription glasses and contact lens solution
Infant formula, bottles, nappies, wipes and nappy rash cream
Pet food and extra water for your pets
Copies of important documents (insurance, identification, bank records) in a waterproof container
Sleeping bag or warm blanket for each person
A complete change of clothing for your climate, and sturdy shoes
Feminine supplies and personal hygiene items
Cups, plates, paper towels and utensils
Books, games or puzzles for children

name: Car kit
items: Cat litter or sand for traction

name: Pet kit
source: Ready.gov, Pets and Animals (public domain): https://www.ready.gov/pets
items: Food for at least a week, in an airtight, waterproof container
Water for at least a week
Collar with ID tag, harness or leash
Vaccination records and other documents in a waterproof container
Litter, litter box, newspaper or bags for waste
A recent photo of you with your pet, in case you are separated

name: First aid kit
source: General list. Adapt it with the training you have.
items: Printed first aid cards (Manual, First Aid Cards)
Tourniquet (only if you are trained to use it)

name: Blackout kit
items: Flashlight or headlamp for each person (not candles)
Appliance thermometers for the fridge and freezer
Backup power plan for medical devices
Carbon monoxide alarm with battery backup
